learningObjectives: Identify the major components of the Cranial Nerves.
Explain how the Cranial Nerves contributes to sensation, regulation or behaviour.
Connect Cranial Nerves function with clinically relevant symptoms.
Use lesion patterns and phenomenology cautiously rather than relying on one-to-one explanations.

anatomy.label: Sensory nerves I, II, VIII
anatomy.detail: Carry special sensory information into the brain.
anatomy.clinical: Loss patterns can indicate peripheral, brainstem or cortical pathology.

anatomy.label: Eye-movement nerves III, IV, VI
anatomy.detail: Drive extraocular muscles and pupillary responses.
anatomy.clinical: Diplopia and anisocoria can signal urgent neurological disease.

anatomy.label: Trigeminal nerve V
anatomy.detail: Carries facial somatosensation and powers chewing muscles.
anatomy.clinical: Neuralgia or sensory loss has strong localising value.

anatomy.label: Facial nerve VII
anatomy.detail: Controls facial expression, taste anteriorly and lacrimal/salivary functions.
anatomy.clinical: Upper versus lower facial weakness helps localise lesions.

anatomy.label: Bulbar nerves IX–XII
anatomy.detail: Coordinate pharyngeal, laryngeal and tongue function.
anatomy.clinical: Dysphagia or dysarthria may indicate medullary or peripheral disease.

quizBank.question: Which component is best described as: Smell, vision and hearing/balance?
quizBank.explanation: Carry special sensory information into the brain.

quizBank.question: Which component is best described as: Coordinate gaze and pupils?
quizBank.explanation: Drive extraocular muscles and pupillary responses.

quizBank.question: Which component is best described as: Facial sensation and mastication?
quizBank.explanation: Carries facial somatosensation and powers chewing muscles.

quizBank.question: Which component is best described as: Expression and taste?
quizBank.explanation: Controls facial expression, taste anteriorly and lacrimal/salivary functions.

quizBank.question: Which component is best described as: Voice, swallowing and tongue?
quizBank.explanation: Coordinate pharyngeal, laryngeal and tongue function.
